class="markdown-body entry-content container-lg" itemprop="text"><div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h1 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">sys1grep — System 1 for your files; uses TypeSafe AI's Jev</h1><a id="user-content-sys1grep--system-1-for-your-files-uses-typesafe-ais-jev" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: sys1grep — System 1 for your files; uses TypeSafe AI's Jev" href="#sys1grep--system-1-for-your-files-uses-typesafe-ais-jev"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><a href="/uehaj/jev-semgrep/blob/main/README.ja.md">日本語版はこちら</a></p>
<p dir="auto">Background and design notes (Japanese): <a href="https://zenn.dev/uehaj/articles/jev-semgrep-grep-by-meaning" rel="nofollow">Jevのキラーアプリ、「意味で探す grep」を作った</a> on Zenn.</p>
<p dir="auto">A grep that finds lines by <strong>what they mean</strong>, not by regular expressions.
Matching is done by <strong>Jev</strong>, the System One model from <a href="https://typesafe.ai/" rel="nofollow">TypeSafe AI</a>.
Jev does not generate text. It answers typed questions with probabilities, so for every line
sys1grep asks "does this line match the meaning <em>network failure</em>?", gets a probability back,
and applies a threshold.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="./sys1grep -n -e &quot;customer is angry or frustrated&quot; tickets.txt"><pre>./sys1grep -n -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>customer is angry or frustrated<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> tickets.txt</pre></div>
<p dir="auto"><a href="https://uehaj.github.io/sys1grep/" rel="nofollow"><img src="/uehaj/jev-semgrep/raw/main/docs/demo.svg" alt="sys1grep demo: a Japanese meaning finds refund requests in six languages; &quot;asking for a refund&quot; vs &quot;about a refund&quot;; -Q finds the answer" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<p dir="auto"><sub>▶ Click the demo, or open <a href="https://uehaj.github.io/sys1grep/" rel="nofollow">uehaj.github.io/sys1grep</a>, for the full demo on the landing page.</sub></p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Zero dependencies. One file, Node.js 20.16+ and <code>fetch</code>.</li>
<li>Fast. 30 lines go into one request, requests run 8 at a time. A 210-line file finishes in under a second.</li>
<li>Meanings combine with AND / OR / NOT.</li>
<li><strong>Language-agnostic.</strong> The meaning and the text can each be in any language. A Japanese meaning finds French, Russian, Chinese and Korean lines alike. No translation step, same speed, same cost.</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Search across languages</h2><a id="user-content-search-across-languages" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Search across languages" href="#search-across-languages"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The meaning and the text do not have to share a language. Jev compares concepts, not words,
so one query finds matching lines in every language the file contains.</p>
<p dir="auto">An <strong>English</strong> meaning finds <strong>Japanese</strong> lines. None of the hits contain "angry" or "frustrated", and two of them are in Japanese:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="$ ./sys1grep -n -e &quot;customer is angry or frustrated&quot; tests/corpus.txt
14:ユーザー山田さんからの問い合わせ: 返金してほしい、商品が壊れていた
16:ユーザー佐藤さんからの問い合わせ: 注文した覚えのない請求が来ています。至急確認してください
18:I want my money back. The item arrived broken and customer service ignored me.
21:Your product ruined my weekend. Never buying from you again.
23:This is the third time I'm writing. Nobody has replied to my previous emails."><pre>$ ./sys1grep -n -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>customer is angry or frustrated<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> tests/corpus.txt
14:ユーザー山田さんからの問い合わせ: 返金してほしい、商品が壊れていた
16:ユーザー佐藤さんからの問い合わせ: 注文した覚えのない請求が来ています。至急確認してください
18:I want my money back. The item arrived broken and customer service ignored me.
21:Your product ruined my weekend. Never buying from you again.
23:This is the third <span class="pl-k">time</span> I<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>m writing. Nobody has replied to my previous emails.</span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">A <strong>Japanese</strong> meaning finds <strong>English</strong> lines, with the same confidence as the Japanese ones:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="$ ./sys1grep -n -p -e &quot;返金の要求&quot; tests/corpus.txt
14:ユーザー山田さんからの問い合わせ: 返金してほしい、商品が壊れていた	[0.97]
18:I want my money back. The item arrived broken and customer service ignored me.	[0.95]"><pre>$ ./sys1grep -n -p -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>返金の要求<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> tests/corpus.txt
14:ユーザー山田さんからの問い合わせ: 返金してほしい、商品が壊れていた	[0.97]
18:I want my money back. The item arrived broken and customer service ignored me.	[0.95]</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">It is not a Japanese/English feature. <code>tests/multi.txt</code> holds refund requests and thank-you notes in French,
Russian, German, Spanish, Chinese and Korean. One Japanese meaning finds all six refund requests; a Russian
meaning does the same:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="$ ./sys1grep -n -p -e &quot;顧客が返金を求めている&quot; tests/multi.txt
1:Je veux être remboursé, le produit est arrivé cassé.	[0.98]
3:Я требую вернуть деньги, товар не работает.	[0.97]
5:Ich möchte mein Geld zurück, das Gerät ist defekt.	[0.97]
7:Quiero un reembolso, el paquete llegó vacío.	[0.97]
9:我要求退款，商品坏了。	[0.97]
11:환불해 주세요. 제품이 고장났어요.	[0.97]

$ ./sys1grep -n -p -e &quot;клиент требует возврат денег&quot; tests/multi.txt
1:Je veux être remboursé, le produit est arrivé cassé.	[0.94]
3:Я требую вернуть деньги, товар не работает.	[0.97]
5:Ich möchte mein Geld zurück, das Gerät ist defekt.	[0.92]
7:Quiero un reembolso, el paquete llegó vacío.	[0.89]
9:我要求退款，商品坏了。	[0.92]
11:환불해 주세요. 제품이 고장났어요.	[0.89]"><pre>$ ./sys1grep -n -p -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>顧客が返金を求めている<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> tests/multi.txt
1:Je veux être remboursé, le produit est arrivé cassé.	[0.98]
3:Я требую вернуть деньги, товар не работает.	[0.97]
5:Ich möchte mein Geld zurück, das Gerät ist defekt.	[0.97]
7:Quiero un reembolso, el paquete llegó vacío.	[0.97]
9:我要求退款，商品坏了。	[0.97]
11:환불해 주세요. 제품이 고장났어요.	[0.97]

$ ./sys1grep -n -p -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>клиент требует возврат денег<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> tests/multi.txt
1:Je veux être remboursé, le produit est arrivé cassé.	[0.94]
3:Я требую вернуть деньги, товар не работает.	[0.97]
5:Ich möchte mein Geld zurück, das Gerät ist defekt.	[0.92]
7:Quiero un reembolso, el paquete llegó vacío.	[0.89]
9:我要求退款，商品坏了。	[0.92]
11:환불해 주세요. 제품이 고장났어요.	[0.89]</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">This makes sys1grep useful for mixed-language logs and ticket dumps, and for teams whose members
query in different languages. One caveat: TypeSafe documents English as the most accurate language,
and in our tests Japanese meanings wobble a little more near the threshold. When a query is borderline,
phrasing the meaning in English is the safer choice.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">How this differs from vector search</h2><a id="user-content-how-this-differs-from-vector-search" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: How this differs from vector search" href="#how-this-differs-from-vector-search"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">If all you want is "lines about X", embedding similarity gives you the same lines. sys1grep differs in
<em>what</em> it judges: not how close a line is to a topic, but whether a <strong>proposition</strong> holds for that line.
Jev reads the line and the question together (a cross-encoder shape), so who did what, negation, and
"asked for" versus "already done" all change the answer. An embedding of the line is fixed before it
ever sees your query, so it can only measure topical closeness.</p>
<p dir="auto">All eight lines below are "about a refund" (the same contrast as <code>tests/contrast.txt</code>, translated to
English as <code>tests/contrast.en.txt</code> — see <a href="#search-across-languages">Search across languages</a> above for
the case where the meaning and the text differ in language). Only two are a customer asking for one:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="$ ./sys1grep -n -p -t 0 -e &quot;customer is asking for a refund&quot; tests/contrast.en.txt
1:I want a refund. The item was broken.	[0.99]
2:The refund has been processed. Please check your account.	[0.11]
3:Our refund policy is within 30 days of purchase.	[0.09]
4:The manager denied the refund request yesterday	[0.17]
5:I demand a full refund immediately	[0.93]
6:Refunds are processed within 5 business days	[0.07]
7:The support agent got angry and hung up the phone.	[0.05]
8:The customer got angry and hung up the phone.	[0.06]"><pre>$ ./sys1grep -n -p -t 0 -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>customer is asking for a refund<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> tests/contrast.en.txt
1:I want a refund. The item was broken.	[0.99]
2:The refund has been processed. Please check your account.	[0.11]
3:Our refund policy is within 30 days of purchase.	[0.09]
4:The manager denied the refund request yesterday	[0.17]
5:I demand a full refund immediately	[0.93]
6:Refunds are processed within 5 business days	[0.07]
7:The support agent got angry and hung up the phone.	[0.05]
8:The customer got angry and hung up the phone.	[0.06]</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Because each meaning yields an independent probability, <strong>logical AND and NOT are plain boolean
operations</strong>, not a trick with set differences or "negative queries":</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="# about a refund, but NOT a customer asking for one → completed, policy, denied, timelines
$ ./sys1grep -n -e &quot;about a refund&quot; -v &quot;the customer is asking for a refund&quot; tests/contrast.en.txt
2:The refund has been processed. Please check your account.
3:Our refund policy is within 30 days of purchase.
4:The manager denied the refund request yesterday
6:Refunds are processed within 5 business days

# angry AND it is the customer, not the staff
$ ./sys1grep -n -e &quot;someone is angry&quot; -a &quot;the customer, not the staff, is the one acting&quot; tests/contrast.en.txt
5:I demand a full refund immediately
8:The customer got angry and hung up the phone."><pre><span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> about a refund, but NOT a customer asking for one → completed, policy, denied, timelines</span>
$ ./sys1grep -n -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>about a refund<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> -v <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>the customer is asking for a refund<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> tests/contrast.en.txt
2:The refund has been processed. Please check your account.
3:Our refund policy is within 30 days of purchase.
4:The manager denied the refund request yesterday
6:Refunds are processed within 5 business days

<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> angry AND it is the customer, not the staff</span>
$ ./sys1grep -n -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>someone is angry<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> -a <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>the customer, not the staff, is the one acting<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> tests/contrast.en.txt
5:I demand a full refund immediately
8:The customer got angry and hung up the phone.</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Line 7, <code>The support agent got angry and hung up the phone.</code>, scores 0.05 on the second meaning and is
excluded, even though it differs from line 8 by one word (<em>support agent</em> vs. <em>customer</em>) — wording an
embedding would place right next to line 8's. (We could not reproduce a cosine-similarity number for
this pair: no embedding-model access was available in this environment, and no prior measurement script
exists in the repository or its history to rerun. The argument stands on the wording alone: an embedding
of line 7 has no way to see that "support agent" changes who the sentence is about.)</p>
<p dir="auto">Two more practical consequences. The probabilities are calibrated, so one threshold (0.5) works across
queries, where cosine scores need top-k or per-query tuning. And there is no index to build: sys1grep reads
the files in front of you. The flip side is that every query pays for the whole corpus again, so for
repeated queries over a large, fixed corpus a vector index is cheaper and faster.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Regex terms</h2><a id="user-content-regex-terms" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Regex terms" href="#regex-terms"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>-e</code>/<code>-a</code>/<code>-v '/pattern/flags'</code> (first and last character <code>/</code>, JavaScript flags) is matched locally,
as a plain regex, with no request at all. It prefilters its AND term: only the lines it holds for
ever ask that term's meanings, so a cheap regex in front of a meaning cuts both the bill and the wait. A line is sent
only if some term's regexes all hold for it (a term with no regex holds for every line), so with
<code>-e '/re/' -a A -e B</code> a line without <code>re</code> is still sent, asked <code>B</code> only. A query of regex terms alone
sends nothing, except that <code>--sentence</code> (<code>=jev</code>, the default) still asks Jev where wrapped lines
break; use <code>--sentence=rules</code> to stay offline. Anything that isn't shaped like <code>/…/flags</code> is still a meaning, so
<code>-e '/etc 以下のファイルを変更している'</code> (no closing <code>/</code>) is unaffected; a meaning that really starts
and ends with <code>/</code> can be written with a leading space to dodge the regex reading.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="$ ./sys1grep -e '/ERROR|FATAL/' app.log                               # no requests at all
$ ./sys1grep -e '/timeout/i' -a '顧客に影響が出ている' app.log         # only lines with &quot;timeout&quot; go to Jev"><pre>$ ./sys1grep -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>/ERROR|FATAL/<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span> app.log                               <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> no requests at all</span>
$ ./sys1grep -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>/timeout/i<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span> -a <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>顧客に影響が出ている<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span> app.log         <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> only lines with "timeout" go to Jev</span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">A regex's named and numbered groups pass to the other meanings of the <em>same</em> AND term as
<code>$&lt;name&gt;</code>, <code>$1</code>-<code>$99</code>, <code>$&amp;</code>, <code>$$</code> — ECMAScript's replacement-pattern syntax
(<code>String.prototype.replace</code>'s <code>GetSubstitution</code>), with one deviation: <code>$&lt;name&gt;</code> naming no group is
an error rather than an empty string (so is a reference to a negated regex's group). A <code>$n</code> naming
no group stays literal, as in ECMAScript, so <code>$100 以上の請求</code> is unaffected.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="$ ./sys1grep -e '/(?&lt;date&gt;\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d) (?&lt;time&gt;\d\d:\d\d)/' \
            -a '$&lt;time&gt; が深夜（0時〜5時）であり、$&lt;date&gt; が週末である' app.log
#   2026-09-19 03:12 ... → asks &quot;03:12 が深夜（0時〜5時）であり、2026-09-19 が週末である&quot;"><pre>$ ./sys1grep -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>/(?&lt;date&gt;\d{4}-\d\d-\d\d) (?&lt;time&gt;\d\d:\d\d)/<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span> \
            -a <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>$&lt;time&gt; が深夜（0時〜5時）であり、$&lt;date&gt; が週末である<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span> app.log
<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span>   2026-09-19 03:12 ... → asks "03:12 が深夜（0時〜5時）であり、2026-09-19 が週末である"</span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Prefer <code>$&lt;name&gt;</code> and single quotes: <code>$&lt;name&gt;</code> survives double quotes in sh/bash/zsh; <code>$1</code>, <code>$time</code>
and <code>${time}</code> don't (the shell expands them itself). <code>-p</code> prints <code>1.00</code>/<code>0.00</code> for a regex term.</p>
<p dir="auto">On a terminal every match of a regex is in grep's match color (bold red), for the terms that held; a negated regex
is never colored. <code>-o</code> prints each match on a line of its own, as <code>grep -o</code>; a line only meanings matched prints
whole, since a meaning has no matching part.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="$ ./sys1grep -o -n -e '/[A-Z]+-\d+/' -a 'the ticket is still open' notes.txt   # the ticket ids, one per line"><pre>$ ./sys1grep -o -n -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>/[A-Z]+-\d+/<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span> -a <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>the ticket is still open<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span> notes.txt   <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> the ticket ids, one per line</span></pre></div>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Sending less</h2><a id="user-content-sending-less" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Sending less" href="#sending-less"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Every line sent to Jev costs money and time, so the cheapest line is the one never sent. From the widest cut
to the narrowest:</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Which files.</strong> <code>-r</code> skips <code>.git</code>, <code>node_modules</code>, binary files, likely secrets and what git ignores;
<a href="#as-a-git-subcommand-git-sys1grep"><code>git sys1grep</code></a> searches tracked files only. <code>--include</code> / <code>--exclude</code>
(file-name globs) and <code>--changed-within</code> (<code>30m</code>, <code>7d</code>, <code>today</code>, <code>this-week</code>, a date) narrow them further.
A meaning that restricts itself to a language or a time of change narrows them by itself: see
<a href="#scope-from-the-meaning">Scope from the meaning</a>.</li>
<li><strong>Which lines.</strong> A <a href="#regex-terms">regex term</a> is matched locally, and only the lines it holds for are asked
its AND term's meanings. Blank lines are never sent.</li>
<li><strong>How many times.</strong> <a href="#one-line-per-template---dedup"><code>--dedup</code></a> judges one line per template: lines that
differ only in ids, numbers, times or paths share one answer.</li>
<li><strong>Check before paying.</strong> <code>--dry-run</code> sends nothing and prints the files, how many lines each would send and
every request with its questions. Its last line estimates the input tokens and, for TypeSafe itself, the price
(<code>~3178 input tokens, ~$0.000133</code>; within about 10%). <code>-i</code> shows the same totals on the terminal and sends only
after <code>y</code>.</li>
</ul>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="$ sys1grep --dry-run -r --include='*.log' --changed-within=today -e '/ERROR|FATAL/' -a 'a customer is affected' logs/"><pre>$ sys1grep --dry-run -r --include=<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>*.log<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span> --changed-within=today -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>/ERROR|FATAL/<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span> -a <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>a customer is affected<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span> logs/</pre></div>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Install</h2><a id="user-content-install" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Install" href="#install"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Two ways to use it: as a command-line tool (this section), or as a Claude Code skill
(see <a href="#use-it-from-claude-code">Use it from Claude Code</a> below). The skill falls back to <code>npx @uehaj/sys1grep</code>,
so if you only use it through Claude Code you can skip the install here entirely and just set the API key.</p>
<p dir="auto">Requires Node.js 20.16 or later. No other dependencies.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="npm install -g @uehaj/sys1grep
sys1grep --help"><pre>npm install -g @uehaj/sys1grep
sys1grep --help</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">To try it without installing, run it through <code>npx</code> (the first run downloads the package, later runs use the cache):</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="npx @uehaj/sys1grep -n -e &quot;customer is angry or frustrated&quot; tickets.txt"><pre>npx @uehaj/sys1grep -n -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>customer is angry or frustrated<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> tickets.txt</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Then give it an API key from the <a href="https://console.typesafe.ai/" rel="nofollow">TypeSafe console</a>. Any one of these works:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="export SYS1GREP_API_KEY=your-key                       # environment variable
echo 'SYS1GREP_API_KEY=your-key' &gt; ~/.config/sys1grep/.env    # per user (mkdir -p first)"><pre><span class="pl-k">export</span> SYS1GREP_API_KEY=your-key                       <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> environment variable</span>
<span class="pl-c1">echo</span> <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>SYS1GREP_API_KEY=your-key<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span> <span class="pl-k">&gt;</span> <span class="pl-k">~</span>/.config/sys1grep/.env    <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> per user (mkdir -p first)</span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Variables already in the environment win; otherwise <code>~/.config/sys1grep/.env</code> fills them in. A <code>.env</code> in the current
directory is never read: it may belong to a repository you just cloned, and could send your key elsewhere through
<code>SYS1GREP_URL</code>. For per-project settings, load a file yourself: <code>node --env-file=.env "$(command -v sys1grep)" ...</code>.
<code>TYPESAFE_API_KEY</code> is accepted too when <code>SYS1GREP_API_KEY</code> is not set.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Default options</h3><a id="user-content-default-options" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Default options" href="#default-options"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>SYS1GREP_OPTS</code> holds options to apply on every call, read like the settings above. It is split on spaces and put in
front of the command line, so the command line wins: a later value counts, and <code>--no-X</code> turns a default flag off.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="export SYS1GREP_OPTS='--level strict -j 8 -n'
sys1grep -e &quot;payment failed&quot; app.log                  # strict, 8 at once, line numbers
sys1grep --level loose --no-n -e &quot;payment failed&quot; app.log"><pre><span class="pl-k">export</span> SYS1GREP_OPTS=<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>--level strict -j 8 -n<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span>
sys1grep -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>payment failed<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> app.log                  <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> strict, 8 at once, line numbers</span>
sys1grep --level loose --no-n -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>payment failed<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> app.log</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">A script calling sys1grep would pick these up too (grep dropped <code>GREP_OPTIONS</code> for that reason). Call it as
<code>SYS1GREP_OPTS= sys1grep ...</code> in scripts.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Other endpoints</h3><a id="user-content-other-endpoints" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Other endpoints" href="#other-endpoints"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The API is configured by exactly three settings: <code>SYS1GREP_API_KEY</code> (or <code>TYPESAFE_API_KEY</code>), <code>SYS1GREP_URL</code> and <code>SYS1GREP_MODEL</code>.
Any endpoint that speaks TypeSafe's <code>POST /v1/systemone</code> works. The key is sent to <code>SYS1GREP_URL</code> as is, so set the
two together. On the command line, <code>--sys1-model=ID</code>, <code>--sys1-url=URL</code> and <code>--sys1-api-key=KEY</code> override
the three. A key given this way shows up in <code>ps</code> and shell history, so prefer <code>~/.config/sys1grep/.env</code> for it.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="# OpenRouter
SYS1GREP_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone SYS1GREP_API_KEY=sk-or-... sys1grep -e ...
# Vercel AI Gateway
SYS1GREP_URL=https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/typesafe/v1/systemone SYS1GREP_MODEL=typesafe-ai/jev SYS1GREP_API_KEY=vck_... sys1grep -e ...
# A compatible server that needs no key: no Authorization header is sent
SYS1GREP_URL=http://localhost:8000/v1/systemone sys1grep -e ..."><pre><span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> OpenRouter</span>
SYS1GREP_URL=https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/systemone SYS1GREP_API_KEY=sk-or-... sys1grep -e ...
<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> Vercel AI Gateway</span>
SYS1GREP_URL=https://ai-gateway.vercel.sh/typesafe/v1/systemone SYS1GREP_MODEL=typesafe-ai/jev SYS1GREP_API_KEY=vck_... sys1grep -e ...
<span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> A compatible server that needs no key: no Authorization header is sent</span>
SYS1GREP_URL=http://localhost:8000/v1/systemone sys1grep -e ...</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">The summary line shows the cost the endpoint reports (<code>usage.cost</code>), or for TypeSafe itself an estimate at list
price marked <code>~</code>.</p>
<p dir="auto">From source: <code>git clone https://github.com/uehaj/sys1grep.git &amp;&amp; cd sys1grep &amp;&amp; npm install -g .</code>,
or run it in place with <code>node sys1grep.mjs ...</code>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Examples</h2><a id="user-content-examples" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Examples" href="#examples"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">All examples run against <a href="/uehaj/jev-semgrep/blob/main/tests/corpus.txt"><code>tests/corpus.txt</code></a>, a 51-line mix of server logs,
support tickets in English and Japanese, source code, SQL and small talk. Where a Japanese line would
otherwise show up in the output below, this section instead uses <a href="/uehaj/jev-semgrep/blob/main/tests/corpus.en.txt"><code>tests/corpus.en.txt</code></a>,
the same 51 lines with the Japanese ones translated to English — the cross-language behaviour itself is
shown once, in <a href="#search-across-languages">Search across languages</a> above.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Find lines by a concept, in any language</h3><a id="user-content-find-lines-by-a-concept-in-any-language" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Find lines by a concept, in any language" href="#find-lines-by-a-concept-in-any-language"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="$ ./sys1grep -n -e &quot;customer is angry or frustrated&quot; tests/corpus.en.txt
14:Inquiry from user Yamada: I want a refund, the item was broken
16:Inquiry from user Sato: I'm being charged for an order I never placed, it looks like fraud, please check urgently
18:I want my money back. The item arrived broken and customer service ignored me.
21:Your product ruined my weekend. Never buying from you again.
23:This is the third time I'm writing. Nobody has replied to my previous emails.
5 of 51 lines matched; 51 sent to Jev in 2 requests, 3054 input tokens, ~$0.000128"><pre>$ ./sys1grep -n -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>customer is angry or frustrated<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> tests/corpus.en.txt
14:Inquiry from user Yamada: I want a refund, the item was broken
16:Inquiry from user Sato: I<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>m being charged for an order I never placed, it looks like fraud, please check urgently</span>
<span class="pl-s">18:I want my money back. The item arrived broken and customer service ignored me.</span>
<span class="pl-s">21:Your product ruined my weekend. Never buying from you again.</span>
<span class="pl-s">23:This is the third time I<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span>m writing. Nobody has replied to my previous emails.
5 of 51 lines matched<span class="pl-k">;</span> 51 sent to Jev <span class="pl-k">in</span> 2 requests, 3054 input tokens, <span class="pl-k">~</span><span class="pl-smi">$0</span>.000128</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">None of these lines contain the words "angry" or "frustrated".</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Lines that answer a question (<code>-Q</code>)</h3><a id="user-content-lines-that-answer-a-question--q" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Lines that answer a question (-Q)" href="#lines-that-answer-a-question--q"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>-e</code> asks whether a line states a meaning. <code>-Q QUESTION</code> (<code>--question</code>) finds lines that answer it instead,
so you can write the question as you would ask it:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="$ echo &quot;The job failed.&quot; | ./sys1grep -e &quot;Did the job succeed?&quot;
$ echo &quot;The job failed.&quot; | ./sys1grep -Q &quot;Did the job succeed?&quot;
The job failed."><pre>$ <span class="pl-c1">echo</span> <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>The job failed.<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> <span class="pl-k">|</span> ./sys1grep -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Did the job succeed?<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>
$ <span class="pl-c1">echo</span> <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>The job failed.<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> <span class="pl-k">|</span> ./sys1grep -Q <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Did the job succeed?<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>
The job failed.</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">As a meaning, "Did the job succeed?" is not what the line says (0.08), so <code>-e</code> finds nothing. As a question,
the line answers it: no, it failed (0.83). A line that <em>asks</em> the question is close to it in meaning but
answers nothing, and for a yes/no question a line that <em>denies</em> it still answers it:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="$ ./sys1grep -n -Q &quot;whether the server is down&quot; tests/intent.txt
5:The server is down.
6:The server is healthy and responding normally.
2 of 17 lines matched; 17 sent to Jev in 1 request, 1087 input tokens, ~$0.000046"><pre>$ ./sys1grep -n -Q <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>whether the server is down<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> tests/intent.txt
5:The server is down.
6:The server is healthy and responding normally.
2 of 17 lines matched<span class="pl-k">;</span> 17 sent to Jev <span class="pl-k">in</span> 1 request, 1087 input tokens, <span class="pl-k">~</span><span class="pl-smi">$0</span>.000046</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Both the confirming line and the denying line match: each settles whether the server is down. <code>Is the server down?</code> does not match, because asking is not answering; <code>-e "asking whether the server is down"</code>
would match it instead. <code>-Q X</code> is shorthand for <code>-e "the line answers: X"</code>, so it combines with <code>-a</code> / <code>-v</code>
/ <code>!</code> and OR's with other terms exactly like <code>-e</code>.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">OR: two meanings, and see the probabilities with <code>-p</code></h3><a id="user-content-or-two-meanings-and-see-the-probabilities-with--p" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: OR: two meanings, and see the probabilities with -p" href="#or-two-meanings-and-see-the-probabilities-with--p"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

<p dir="auto">The bracket shows one probability per meaning, in the order given. Use it to pick a threshold.</p>
<p dir="auto">With <code>--color</code> (on by default in a terminal) the probabilities are colored against the thresholds:
green at or above <code>-t</code>, red below <code>-T</code>, yellow in between. Line numbers and file names use grep's colors.</p>
<p dir="auto"><a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="/uehaj/jev-semgrep/blob/main/docs/color.svg"><img src="/uehaj/jev-semgrep/raw/main/docs/color.svg" alt="colored output: line numbers in green, probabilities in green or red" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">AND NOT: network errors, excluding retries</h3><a id="user-content-and-not-network-errors-excluding-retries" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: AND NOT: network errors, excluding retries" href="#and-not-network-errors-excluding-retries"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Strictness presets</h3><a id="user-content-strictness-presets" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Strictness presets" href="#strictness-presets"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="$ ./sys1grep --level strict -n -e &quot;a security risk or dangerous destructive operation&quot; tests/corpus.en.txt
