<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Recursive search and file names only</h3><a id="user-content-recursive-search-and-file-names-only" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Recursive search and file names only" href="#recursive-search-and-file-names-only"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="$ ./sys1grep -r -n -e &quot;customer is asking for a refund&quot; tests/tickets/
tests/tickets/a.txt:7:Ticket #16: I want a refund, the item was broken.
tests/tickets/sub/b.txt:1:The customer wants a refund for the broken lamp.

$ ./sys1grep -rl -e &quot;customer is asking for a refund&quot; tests/tickets/
tests/tickets/a.txt
tests/tickets/sub/b.txt"><pre>$ ./sys1grep -r -n -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>customer is asking for a refund<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> tests/tickets/
tests/tickets/a.txt:7:Ticket <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span>16: I want a refund, the item was broken.</span>
tests/tickets/sub/b.txt:1:The customer wants a refund <span class="pl-k">for</span> the broken lamp.

$ ./sys1grep -rl -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>customer is asking for a refund<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> tests/tickets/
tests/tickets/a.txt
tests/tickets/sub/b.txt</pre></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>-r</code> walks directories in sorted order and skips <code>.git</code>, <code>node_modules</code>, <code>.ssh</code>, <code>.aws</code>, <code>.gnupg</code>, <code>.kube</code>,
<code>.docker</code>, binary files (a NUL byte in the first 8 KB, or a PDF; UTF-16 with a BOM is read as text) and files
that usually hold secrets (<code>.env*</code>, <code>.netrc</code>, <code>.npmrc</code>, <code>.pypirc</code>, <code>.pgpass</code>, <code>.git-credentials</code>, <code>*.pem</code>,
<code>*.key</code>, <code>*.p12</code>, <code>*.pfx</code>, <code>*.jks</code>, <code>*.keystore</code>, <code>id_rsa*</code> and friends; names compared without case). <strong>Every line that is searched is sent to the TypeSafe API</strong>, so point <code>-r</code> at a directory
you mean to scan. Inside a git repository, <code>-r</code> also skips what git ignores (<code>.gitignore</code>, <code>.git/info/exclude</code>, the
global excludes file), so build output and local files stay home; a tracked file is searched even if it matches.
A file named explicitly on the command line is always searched, even if it matches the skip list or is ignored;
so is a directory that git ignores, when you name it (<code>sys1grep -r -e ... dist</code>). <code>-l</code> prints each
matching file once, in the order matches are found, and works with or without <code>-r</code>. <code>-c</code> prints the number of
matching lines per file instead.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Scope from the meaning</h3><a id="user-content-scope-from-the-meaning" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Scope from the meaning" href="#scope-from-the-meaning"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">A meaning that restricts its matches to some kind of file can only match in such files. With <code>-r</code> and
<code>git sys1grep</code>, each meaning first asks Jev, in one small request, a yes / no per candidate, and a yes at 0.6 or
more narrows the files before anything else is sent. The rest is never read or sent. Each scope is reported on
stderr with Jev's answer, so a wrong one is visible:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="$ sys1grep -r -e 'Python でリトライ処理を書いている箇所' .
sys1grep: scope: *.py *.pyi *.pyw (from &quot;Python files: 0.94&quot;)
sys1grep: scope: 12 of 340 files
$ sys1grep -r -e '昨日変えた箇所で認証を扱っている' src/
sys1grep: scope: modified since 2026-09-25 00:00 (from &quot;what was changed yesterday: 0.91&quot;)
sys1grep: scope: 3 of 120 files"><pre>$ sys1grep -r -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>Python でリトライ処理を書いている箇所<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span> <span class="pl-c1">.</span>
sys1grep: scope: <span class="pl-k">*</span>.py <span class="pl-k">*</span>.pyi <span class="pl-k">*</span>.pyw (from <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>Python files: 0.94<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>)
sys1grep: scope: 12 of 340 files
$ sys1grep -r -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>昨日変えた箇所で認証を扱っている<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span> src/
sys1grep: scope: modified since 2026-09-25 00:00 (from <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>what was changed yesterday: 0.91<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>)
sys1grep: scope: 3 of 120 files</pre></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li><strong>Language or format</strong>: 26 candidates (Python, JavaScript, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java, Kotlin, Ruby, PHP, C, C++,
C#, Swift, Scala, R, shell script, SQL, HTML, CSS, Markdown, YAML, JSON, TOML, XML, Dockerfile, Makefile), with
GitHub Linguist's extensions and file names. Several yes answers are alternatives ("JavaScript か TypeScript").</li>
<li><strong>Time of change</strong>: 14 spans: the last minute, the last hour, today, yesterday, the last 1 / 2 / 3 / 7 / 30 days,
this month, last week, last month, the last year, this fiscal year (from April 1). The narrowest span answered
yes is taken, by its start only: a file changed yesterday may have been modified again today.</li>
<li><strong>Place</strong>: test code (<code>tests/ test/ __tests__/ spec/ e2e/</code>, <code>test_*.py *_test.* *.test.* *.spec.* *Test.java *_spec.rb</code>, and every <code>*.rs</code>: Rust keeps unit tests inside the file), database migrations (<code>*migrat*</code>, Flyway's
<code>V1__*.sql</code>), the README, the changelog (<code>CHANGELOG* CHANGES* HISTORY* NEWS*</code>), documentation (<code>*.md *.rst *.adoc *.txt</code>, <code>docs/</code>), source code (whatever is not documentation, so languages missing from the dictionary still
count) and logs (<code>*.log *.log.N *.out *.err</code>, <code>logs/</code>), by the path conventions of JS, Python, Go, Java, Ruby, Rust
and PHP. Several places are alternatives ("README か CHANGELOG に").</li>
<li><strong>git</strong>: in a repository, a time goes by commits: a committed file needs a commit at or after the start (the
committer date; a checkout sets every mtime to now), an uncommitted one its mtime. States: uncommitted (worktree
and index against HEAD, and untracked files), staged, untracked, this branch (since it left <code>origin/HEAD</code>, <code>main</code>
or <code>master</code>), not pushed (<code>@{upstream}..HEAD</code>, else commits on no remote branch), and mine (<code>user.email</code>'s
commits and the uncommitted files). Authors: the 30 with the most commits (<code>git shortlog</code>), each a candidate by
name and e-mail; a yes narrows to every file a commit of theirs touched. Outside a repository none of these is
asked, and a time goes by the mtime.</li>
<li>Jev reads the whole meaning, in any language: "案A、B、Cで比較" is not about C files, and a date quoted in a
comment is not when the file changed. Nothing is extracted from the text; the candidates are fixed.</li>
<li><strong>Per term.</strong> <code>-e A -e B</code> still searches B in the files A's scope leaves out; within an AND term, and across
categories ("Python のテストコード"), the scopes intersect. Negated meanings (<code>-v</code>, <code>!</code>) are not asked. The
meaning is sent unchanged.</li>
<li>The question costs one small request per meaning, sent only when <code>-r</code> / <code>git sys1grep</code> found something to
narrow, and after <code>-i</code>'s answer. <code>--dry-run</code> shows it as <code>[scope]</code>. As with <code>--include</code>, with <code>-r</code> a file named on
the command line and stdin are never narrowed, and <code>git sys1grep</code>'s pathspecs are narrowed like the rest. <code>--no-auto-scope</code> turns it off (<code>--auto-scope</code> turns it back on).</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">As a git subcommand (<code>git sys1grep</code>)</h3><a id="user-content-as-a-git-subcommand-git-sys1grep" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: As a git subcommand (git sys1grep)" href="#as-a-git-subcommand-git-sys1grep"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>npm install -g</code> also installs <code>git-sys1grep</code>, so git runs it as <code>git sys1grep</code>. Like <code>git grep</code>, it searches only
the files git tracks (ignored files and build output are never sent), and FILE arguments are pathspecs relative
to the current directory.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="$ cd tests &amp;&amp; git sys1grep -l -e &quot;customer is asking for a refund&quot; fixture.txt tickets
fixture.txt
tickets/a.txt
tickets/sub/b.txt"><pre>$ <span class="pl-c1">cd</span> tests <span class="pl-k">&amp;&amp;</span> git sys1grep -l -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>customer is asking for a refund<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> fixture.txt tickets
fixture.txt
tickets/a.txt
tickets/sub/b.txt</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Without FILE it searches every tracked file under the current directory. The <code>-r</code> skip list (<code>.env*</code>, keys, ...)
applies even to tracked files. <code>--include</code>, <code>--exclude</code> and <code>--changed-within</code> filter the tracked files, those named
by a pathspec included. <code>--changed-within</code> reads the working tree's modification times, not git history: right after
a clone or a checkout, every file it wrote counts as just changed. For help use <code>git sys1grep -h</code>: git takes <code>--help</code> itself and looks for a man page.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Everything that is <em>not</em> something</h3><a id="user-content-everything-that-is-not-something" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Everything that is not something" href="#everything-that-is-not-something"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="./sys1grep -v &quot;a timestamped server log line&quot; mixed.txt   # like grep -v
./sys1grep -e &quot;source code or SQL&quot; -v &quot;SQL&quot; src.txt       # code, but not SQL
cat app.log | ./sys1grep -e &quot;the deploy failed or was rolled back&quot;"><pre>./sys1grep -v <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>a timestamped server log line<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> mixed.txt   <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> like grep -v</span>
./sys1grep -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>source code or SQL<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> -v <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>SQL<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> src.txt       <span class="pl-c"><span class="pl-c">#</span> code, but not SQL</span>
cat app.log <span class="pl-k">|</span> ./sys1grep -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>the deploy failed or was rolled back<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span></pre></div>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Records that span several lines (<code>-z</code>)</h3><a id="user-content-records-that-span-several-lines--z" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Records that span several lines (-z)" href="#records-that-span-several-lines--z"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">The unit of judgement is a line. That is right for logs and source, and wrong when one record spans
several lines. <code>-z</code> makes the unit a NUL-terminated record instead, exactly as in <code>grep -z</code>, so it pairs
with the tools that already emit records: <code>git log -z</code>, <code>find -print0</code>, <code>xargs -0</code>.</p>
<p dir="auto">A proposition like "this commit changes user-visible behaviour" is true of a whole commit, not of any one
line in it:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="$ git log -z --format='%h %s %b' | ./sys1grep -z -n -e &quot;the change alters user-visible behaviour&quot; -v &quot;documentation only&quot;
7:21120e9 Revert &quot;feat: ship the /sys1grep Claude Code skill&quot; ...
8:51ae333 feat: ship the /sys1grep Claude Code skill"><pre>$ git log -z --format=<span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>%h %s %b<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span> <span class="pl-k">|</span> ./sys1grep -z -n -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>the change alters user-visible behaviour<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> -v <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>documentation only<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span>
7:21120e9 Revert <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>feat: ship the /sys1grep Claude Code skill<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> ...
8:51ae333 feat: ship the /sys1grep Claude Code skill</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Matching records are printed NUL-terminated too, so pipe them through <code>tr '\0' '\n'</code> to read them.
File names (<code>-l</code>) and counts (<code>-c</code>) stay on newlines, as they do in grep. With <code>-z</code>, <code>-n</code> numbers records,
<code>-A</code> / <code>-B</code> / <code>-C</code> count neighbouring records, and <code>--chunk</code> counts records per request.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">One sentence at a time (<code>--sentence</code>)</h3><a id="user-content-one-sentence-at-a-time---sentence" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: One sentence at a time (--sentence)" href="#one-sentence-at-a-time---sentence"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>--sentence</code> judges each sentence instead of each line. The output is still lines, as in grep: every line a
matching sentence touches is printed, and on a terminal the sentence itself is in bold yellow (a regex match inside it, in grep's bold red).
Wrapped lines are joined before splitting, so a sentence that runs over several lines is judged as one.
<a href="/uehaj/jev-semgrep/blob/main/tests/prose.txt"><code>tests/prose.txt</code></a> wraps an English paragraph and a Japanese one:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="$ ./sys1grep -n --sentence -e &quot;the author admits they made a mistake&quot; tests/prose.txt
1:I should have checked the input
2:before shipping, and that was my
3:mistake. Next time I will add a test"><pre>$ ./sys1grep -n --sentence -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>the author admits they made a mistake<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> tests/prose.txt
1:I should have checked the input
2:before shipping, and that was my
3:mistake. Next <span class="pl-k">time</span> I will add a <span class="pl-c1">test</span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">The sentence starts on line 1 and ends at <code>mistake.</code> on line 3; only that part is colored, not
<code>Next time I will add a test</code>, which is judged separately and does not match.</p>
<p dir="auto">On a terminal, with both meanings and <code>-C 3</code> for context, the colors show where each sentence starts and ends
inside a line: lines 3 and 9 are colored only up to the end of the matching sentence, and lines 4-7 are context (<code>-</code>):</p>
<p dir="auto"><a target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" href="/uehaj/jev-semgrep/blob/main/docs/sentence.svg"><img src="/uehaj/jev-semgrep/raw/main/docs/sentence.svg" alt="--sentence -C 3 --color: the matching sentences in bold yellow, up to mistake. on line 3 and 返金してほしいです。 on line 9; lines 4 to 7 as context" style="max-width: 100%;"></a></p>
<p dir="auto"><code>-o</code> prints only the matching sentences, one per line, as <code>grep -o</code> prints only the matching part.
<code>-n</code> then gives the line where the sentence starts. Japanese is joined without a space, as are Chinese,
Thai, Lao, Khmer, Myanmar and Tibetan, which do not put spaces between words:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="$ ./sys1grep -n -o --sentence -e &quot;the author admits they made a mistake&quot; -e &quot;customer is asking for a refund&quot; tests/prose.txt
1:I should have checked the input before shipping, and that was my mistake.
8:先週買った掃除機が初日から動かないので返金してほしいです。"><pre>$ ./sys1grep -n -o --sentence -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>the author admits they made a mistake<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>customer is asking for a refund<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> tests/prose.txt
1:I should have checked the input before shipping, and that was my mistake.
8:先週買った掃除機が初日から動かないので返金してほしいです。</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Without <code>-o</code>, <code>-c</code> counts lines and <code>-A</code> / <code>-B</code> / <code>-C</code> count lines, as usual. With <code>-o</code> they count sentences.
With <code>-z</code>, each record is split on its own and matching records are printed whole.</p>
<p dir="auto">Jev finds a matching sentence inside a long line on its own, so <code>--sentence</code> is not needed for accuracy.
Use it to see which sentence matched, to get the sentences with <code>-o</code>, and when AND should hold within one
sentence: the expression is evaluated per sentence. For the same reason <code>-v X</code> alone prints every line
with at least one sentence that is not X; to find lines that are not X as a whole, leave <code>--sentence</code> off.</p>
<p dir="auto">Japanese and Chinese entries often end without <code>。</code>: a chat message, a support ticket, a memo line. Joining
them would glue separate entries into one "sentence". So by default (<code>--sentence</code>, the same as
<code>--sentence=jev</code>) sys1grep asks Jev about each unpunctuated break next to a script written without word
spaces: "does this line break end a sentence or entry, or is it a wrap inside a sentence?" It sends 30 lines
per request with one yes/no per break, and keeps the lines apart when the answer is 0.7 or more. On
<a href="/uehaj/jev-semgrep/blob/main/tests/corpus.txt"><code>tests/corpus.txt</code></a> this keeps the four one-line Japanese tickets apart, so
<code>--sentence</code> finds the same refund requests (lines 14 and 18) as a line-by-line search, where the rules alone
merged the tickets and missed line 18. The extra requests cost about as much as one more meaning; use
<code>--sentence=rules</code> to skip them. Breaks between English lines are never asked: joining them keeps a space,
and the full stop still ends the sentence.</p>
<p dir="auto">Where a newline cannot be inside a sentence, lines are not joined: at a blank line, next to brackets or
<code>;</code> (JSON, code), and before a line starting with <code>-</code> <code>*</code> <code>+</code> <code>#</code> <code>&gt;</code> <code>"</code> or a digit (list items,
headings, quotes, numbers, timestamps). So JSONL keeps one line per record and each line is split on its
own. Sentences are cut by <code>Intl.Segmenter</code> (<a href="https://unicode.org/reports/tr29/" rel="nofollow">Unicode UAX #29</a>),
which splits at <code>.</code> <code>!</code> <code>?</code> <code>。</code> <code>！</code> <code>？</code> but also after abbreviations such as <code>Mr.</code>. Logs are not prose:
consecutive log lines that start with a letter, such as <code>WARN ...</code> after <code>ERROR ...</code>, get joined.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">One line per template (<code>--dedup</code>)</h3><a id="user-content-one-line-per-template---dedup" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: One line per template (--dedup)" href="#one-line-per-template---dedup"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Cost is proportional to the text sent, and machine-generated logs are mostly one skeleton with a different
id or number in it. <code>--dedup</code> masks ids, hashes, numbers, dates and times, paths and URLs, groups lines by
the result, sends one line per group and reuses its answer for the rest. What is sent is that line's
original text, and every line is printed as itself:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="$ ./sys1grep --dedup -n -e &quot;a request failed&quot; app.log
1:worker request 3fa9c1e27b failed: connection reset
2:worker request 88d0e41a5c failed: connection reset
4:worker request 0b7f2a9e13 failed: connection reset
3 of 6 lines matched; 4 sent to Jev (2 folded by --dedup, ~235 input tokens / ~$0.000010 saved, 21%) in 2 requests, 907 input tokens, ~$0.000038"><pre>$ ./sys1grep --dedup -n -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>a request failed<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> app.log
1:worker request 3fa9c1e27b failed: connection reset
2:worker request 88d0e41a5c failed: connection reset
4:worker request 0b7f2a9e13 failed: connection reset
3 of 6 lines matched<span class="pl-k">;</span> 4 sent to Jev (2 folded by --dedup, <span class="pl-k">~</span>235 input tokens / <span class="pl-k">~</span><span class="pl-smi">$0</span>.000010 saved, 21%) <span class="pl-k">in</span> 2 requests, 907 input tokens, <span class="pl-k">~</span><span class="pl-smi">$0</span>.000038</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Whether a value may be folded depends on the meaning: a number decides "disk usage is above 90%", a time
decides "happened at night". So Jev is first asked, one small request per meaning, which kinds of value
could change a match, and those kinds are kept apart (one of the two requests above). With
<code>-e "disk usage is above 90%"</code> the same file keeps <code>95%</code> and <code>12%</code> apart and prints only <code>5:disk usage 95%</code>.</p>
<p dir="auto">Measured on real logs, with nothing kept: a 43,071-line system log folds into 550 templates (1.2% of the
bytes), <code>install.log</code> to 21.1%, a Claude Code transcript (jsonl) only to 56.8%. It is for machine-generated
logs; prose has no shared skeleton, and a meaning that reads a timestamp folds almost nothing. With <code>-z</code> or
<code>--sentence</code> the records or sentences fold instead of lines.</p>
<p dir="auto">After a search, the summary line says what the folding saved: <code>(2 folded by --dedup, ~235 input tokens / ~$0.000010 saved, 21%)</code> above. It estimates what the folded lines would have cost as requests of their own and subtracts
what the value questions cost. On a small file or on prose, the result can be negative.</p>
<p dir="auto">To see how far your own logs fold before paying for a search, <code>node scripts/dedup-measure.mjs FILE...</code>
counts lines, templates and the share of bytes sent, offline, with the same masks; <code>--keep=num,time</code> shows
a meaning that keeps those kinds apart.</p>
<p dir="auto">The request's other lines are each line's context (#9), and <code>--dedup</code> changes them, so a line near the
threshold can be judged differently than in a full pass.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">A summary instead of the lines (<code>--summarize</code>)</h3><a id="user-content-a-summary-instead-of-the-lines---summarize" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: A summary instead of the lines (--summarize)" href="#a-summary-instead-of-the-lines---summarize"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">When many lines match, what you want is often the gist: what they say about the meaning you searched for.
<code>--summarize</code> pipes what sys1grep would print to <code>claude -p --model haiku</code> (no tools, no settings, no CLAUDE.md),
asks it to summarize the lines as they bear on the meanings, and prints its answer instead of the lines.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="$ sys1grep -r -n --summarize -e &quot;the API key is read from a file&quot; .
The key is read in sys1grep.mjs:22 from ~/.config/sys1grep/.env, never from ./.env (sys1grep.mjs:18), ..."><pre>$ sys1grep -r -n --summarize -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>the API key is read from a file<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> <span class="pl-c1">.</span>
The key is <span class="pl-c1">read</span> <span class="pl-k">in</span> sys1grep.mjs:22 from <span class="pl-k">~</span>/.config/sys1grep/.env, never from ./.env (sys1grep.mjs:18), ...</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">The expensive model reads only what Jev kept. Asking why <code>./.env</code> is no longer read of this repository's
<code>git log</code> (168 commits), Claude's input fell from 22,059 tokens to 1,356, the total cost with Jev's from
$0.094 to $0.013, with the same answer (#69). It pays when the answer sits in a few lines.</p>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>The matching lines leave the machine a second time, to Anthropic.</li>
<li><code>-n</code>, <code>-A/-B/-C</code>, <code>-p</code> and file names go in as they would print; colors never do. No match runs nothing (exit 1).</li>
<li><code>SYS1GREP_SUMMARIZER</code> picks the TOOL of a bare <code>--summarize</code> (only <code>claude</code> so far), <code>SYS1GREP_SUMMARIZER_MODEL</code> its model.</li>
<li><code>-q</code>, <code>-l</code> and <code>-c</code> print no lines, so they cannot be combined with it.</li>
<li>With <code>--dedup</code>, the TOOL gets what Jev got: each template's representative once, marked <code>(×N like it)</code>,
not every line its answer was reused for.</li>
<li>More than 200 KB (about 50k tokens) is not sent at all: exit 2, with the size, before the TOOL is paid.
It is never cut short, since a summary of the first part would read as a summary of all of it.</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Use it from Claude Code</h2><a id="user-content-use-it-from-claude-code" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Use it from Claude Code" href="#use-it-from-claude-code"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">There is a Claude Code skill that runs sys1grep for you: describe what you are looking for in plain words
and it builds the expression, runs the search and reports <code>file:line</code> hits. It is published in the
<a href="https://github.com/uehaj/uehaj-marketplace"><code>uehaj/uehaj-marketplace</code></a> marketplace as the <code>uehaj</code> plugin.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="claude plugin marketplace add uehaj/uehaj-marketplace
claude plugin install uehaj@uehaj-marketplace"><pre>claude plugin marketplace add uehaj/uehaj-marketplace
claude plugin install uehaj@uehaj-marketplace</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">No separate install of the command-line tool is needed: the skill uses <code>sys1grep</code> from your PATH if present,
otherwise <code>npx @uehaj/sys1grep</code>. Only the API key has to be set (see <a href="#install">Install</a>).</p>
<p dir="auto">Then, inside Claude Code:</p>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="/uehaj:sys1grep customer is asking for a refund tickets/*.txt
/uehaj:sys1grep a fix that shipped without a test git log --oneline -200"><pre class="notranslate"><code>/uehaj:sys1grep customer is asking for a refund tickets/*.txt
/uehaj:sys1grep a fix that shipped without a test git log --oneline -200
</code></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Claude Code installs plugins, not single skills. If you want just this one skill, the
<a href="https://skills.sh/" rel="nofollow">skills CLI</a> copies it into <code>~/.claude/skills/</code> and it is invoked as <code>/sys1grep</code>:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="npx skills add uehaj/uehaj-marketplace --skill sys1grep -a claude-code -g"><pre>npx skills add uehaj/uehaj-marketplace --skill sys1grep -a claude-code -g</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">The skill writes the meaning in English, picks <code>-e</code> / <code>-a</code> / <code>-v</code> for AND / OR / NOT, adds <code>-n</code>, narrows large
directories to files worth paying for, and re-runs with <code>--level loose</code> or <code>strict</code> when the first result looks off.
The API key and endpoint are read the same way as on the command line (<code>SYS1GREP_API_KEY</code>, <code>~/.config/sys1grep/.env</code>).</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Usage</h2><a id="user-content-usage" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Usage" href="#usage"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<div class="snippet-clipboard-content notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="usage: sys1grep [OPTION]... -e MEANING|-Q QUESTION [-a MEANING] [-v MEANING]... [FILE...]

  -v MEANING   AND NOT onto the preceding -e/-Q term.  -e A -v B       =  A and not B
               At the front it is a bare negation.  -v B            =  not B  (like grep -v)
  !MEANING     a leading ! negates just that meaning, in -e / -Q / -a / -v alike
               -e A -e '!B'  =  A or not B.   -a '!C' is the same as -v C
  --level=LEVEL strictness preset, sets both thresholds (default normal)
                 loose  : -t 0.3 -T 0.7  catch more, accept some noise
                 normal : -t 0.5 -T 0.5
                 strict : -t 0.7 -T 0.3  only confident matches
  -t THRESH    positive threshold: match when probability &gt;= THRESH (overrides --level)
  -T THRESH    negative threshold: &quot;not X&quot; when probability &lt; THRESH (overrides --level)
               with -t 0.6 -T 0.3 a line at 0.3..0.6 matches neither X nor not-X
  -r           recurse into directories (current directory when FILE is omitted);
               skips .git, node_modules, binary files, likely secrets and what git ignores
  --include=GLOB, --exclude=GLOB  with -r and git sys1grep, only files whose name matches GLOB, or not
               (with -r a file named on the command line is always searched; git sys1grep's pathspecs are filtered)
  --changed-within=WHEN  with -r and git sys1grep, only files modified within 30m / 2h / 7d / 2w, since a date
               or date-time, today, this-week or this-month
  --no-auto-scope  do not narrow those files by what a meaning says about them (see Scope from the meaning);
               --auto-scope turns it back on
  -l           print only the names of files with a match, not the lines
  -H, --with-filename  prefix file names even for a single file; --no-filename never prefixes them
  -A NUM       print NUM lines of trailing context after each match (context lines use - as separator)
  -B NUM       print NUM lines of leading context before each match
  -C NUM       print NUM lines of context before and after (-A NUM -B NUM)
  -c           print only a count of matching lines per file (like grep -c)
  -q, --quiet  print nothing, stop at the first match; exit 0 on a match, even after an error (like grep -q)
  --chunk=LINES lines per request (default 30)
               Lines in one request are each other's context, so a small chunk changes verdicts
               on ambiguous lines, not just speed
  -j N         concurrent requests (default 8)
  -n           print line numbers

  -p           print each meaning's probability at the end of the line
  --dry-run    send nothing; print the endpoint, each file searched and each request with its questions
  --verbose    print the same to stderr while searching
  -i, --interactive  show what --dry-run would send, and search only after y on the terminal

<p dir="auto">Without FILE, stdin is read. With several files, output is prefixed with <code>file:</code>.
Exit codes follow grep: 0 matched, 1 no match, 2 error (bad arguments, unreadable file, API failure).</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Expression grammar</h3><a id="user-content-expression-grammar" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Expression grammar" href="#expression-grammar"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>-e</code> starts an OR term. <code>-a</code> and <code>-v</code> extend the previous term with AND and AND NOT.
A leading <code>!</code> on a meaning negates just that meaning (quote it, <code>!</code> is history expansion in most shells).</p>

</tr>
<tr>

</tr>

<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">How it works</h2><a id="user-content-how-it-works" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: How it works" href="#how-it-works"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ol dir="auto">
<li>Non-blank lines are cut into chunks of 30 lines (with a character cap).</li>
<li>Each chunk goes into <code>state</code> as an object <code>{"L000": "line 1", "L001": "line 2", ...}</code>,
and one <code>noul</code> (yes/no probability) question per line × meaning goes into the same request.</li>
<li>Up to 8 requests run concurrently. Output is printed in file order.</li>
<li>Per line, each meaning's probability is thresholded to a boolean and the AND / OR / NOT expression is evaluated.</li>
</ol>
<p dir="auto">Lines sent together are each other's context: Jev judges a line against what the rest of the chunk shows
is normal in the file. Clear matches and non-matches hold, but ambiguous lines can move. Where the chunk
boundaries fall barely matters (moving them by 15 lines at <code>--chunk 30</code> flipped 1 line in 200 of a log), but
judging a line with little of its file around it does: <code>--chunk 1</code> flipped 18 of the same 200, and those
solitary verdicts were the less reliable ones (#9). So <code>--chunk</code> changes results, not just speed, and a
very short input is judged with little context whatever <code>--chunk</code> says. One line at a time is also slow
(30 lines in one request take about 0.2 s, one line at a time about 7 s).
Very large chunks start losing lines near the threshold, hence the default of 30.
Probabilities drift by about ±0.05 between runs. Use <code>-p</code> when tuning thresholds.</p>
<p dir="auto">Pricing is $0.042 per million input tokens (September 2026). A 30-line chunk with two meanings is about
3,000 tokens. Throughput is bounded by the rate limit of 1,200 requests per minute, roughly 36,000 lines
per minute at the defaults.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Tests</h2><a id="user-content-tests" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Tests" href="#tests"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto"><code>tests/</code> holds an LLM-as-judge test. Each of the 10 cases in <code>tests/cases.json</code> runs against
<code>tests/corpus.txt</code> (51 lines). Claude (<code>claude -p</code>) decides which lines truly match each meaning;
the runner evaluates the boolean expression on those verdicts and compares with sys1grep's output,
reporting precision and recall. It also sweeps <code>-t</code> × <code>-T</code> in 0.05 steps and reports the best pair.</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="node --no-warnings tests/judge.mts [--model sonnet] [--rejudge]"><pre>node --no-warnings tests/judge.mts [--model sonnet] [--rejudge]</pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Judge verdicts are cached in <code>tests/verdicts.json</code>; later runs do not call the judge.
The result is written to <code>tests/report.md</code>. Latest: precision 0.94, recall 0.98.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">Limits</h2><a id="user-content-limits" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: Limits" href="#limits"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<ul dir="auto">
<li>Every searched line is sent to api.typesafe.ai. Do not run it over files you would not upload there.</li>
<li>Blank lines are not sent; they count as probability 0 for every meaning, so <code>-v X</code> prints them and <code>-e X</code> never does.</li>
<li>Lines are truncated to 2,000 characters before sending.</li>
<li>The maximum number of questions per request is undocumented; 420 worked.</li>
<li>429 / 529 are retried up to 6 times with exponential backoff.</li>
<li>Accuracy is best in English. Japanese works but is noisier.</li>
</ul>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h2 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">FAQ</h2><a id="user-content-faq" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: FAQ" href="#faq"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Some options were left out because a standard tool in front of sys1grep already does the job. These are the
combinations.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">How do I judge a whole paragraph as one unit? Why is there no <code>--paragraph</code>?</h3><a id="user-content-how-do-i-judge-a-whole-paragraph-as-one-unit-why-is-there-no---paragraph" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: How do I judge a whole paragraph as one unit? Why is there no --paragraph?" href="#how-do-i-judge-a-whole-paragraph-as-one-unit-why-is-there-no---paragraph"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Join each paragraph into one line first. <code>fmt</code> joins the lines of a paragraph and keeps the blank lines
between paragraphs:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="fmt -w 100000 essay.txt | sys1grep -n -e &quot;the author admits they made a mistake&quot;"><pre>fmt -w 100000 essay.txt <span class="pl-k">|</span> sys1grep -n -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>the author admits they made a mistake<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Each output line is then a whole paragraph, and <code>-n</code> counts the lines of <code>fmt</code>'s output, not of the file.
<code>fmt</code> puts a space where it joins two Japanese lines; Jev reads through it. To judge sentences across
wrapped lines you need neither: <code>--sentence</code> already joins them.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">How do I search a JSONL chat log one message at a time?</h3><a id="user-content-how-do-i-search-a-jsonl-chat-log-one-message-at-a-time" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: How do I search a JSONL chat log one message at a time?" href="#how-do-i-search-a-jsonl-chat-log-one-message-at-a-time"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Take the text out with <code>jq</code> and end each message with NUL, then judge records with <code>-z</code>:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="jq -j '.content + &quot;\u0000&quot;' chat.jsonl | sys1grep -z -n --sentence -e &quot;the customer is asking for a refund&quot; | tr '\0' '\n'"><pre>jq -j <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>.content + "\u0000"<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span> chat.jsonl <span class="pl-k">|</span> sys1grep -z -n --sentence -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>the customer is asking for a refund<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> <span class="pl-k">|</span> tr <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>\0<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span> <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>\n<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">Adjust <code>.content</code> to where your log keeps the text. Each message becomes one record, so a sentence never
runs into the next speaker's message, and the JSON punctuation is not sent. <code>-n</code> numbers messages. The file
also works as is, one JSON object per line; <code>jq</code> just gives cleaner units.</p>
<div class="markdown-heading" dir="auto"><h3 tabindex="-1" class="heading-element" dir="auto">My records are separated by something other than NUL. Why is there no <code>--record-separator</code>?</h3><a id="user-content-my-records-are-separated-by-something-other-than-nul-why-is-there-no---record-separator" class="anchor" aria-label="Permalink: My records are separated by something other than NUL. Why is there no --record-separator?" href="#my-records-are-separated-by-something-other-than-nul-why-is-there-no---record-separator"><svg data-component="Octicon" class="octicon octicon-link" viewBox="0 0 16 16" version="1.1" width="16" height="16" aria-hidden="true"><path d="m7.775 3.275 1.25-1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1 4.95 4.95l-2.5 2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1-4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1 .018-1.042.751.751 0 0 1 1.042-.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l2.5-2.5a2.002 2.002 0 0 0-2.83-2.83l-1.25 1.25a.751.751 0 0 1-1.042-.018.751.751 0 0 1-.018-1.042Zm-4.69 9.64a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 2.83 0l1.25-1.25a.751.751 0 0 1 1.042.018.751.751 0 0 1 .018 1.042l-1.25 1.25a3.5 3.5 0 1 1-4.95-4.95l2.5-2.5a3.5 3.5 0 0 1 4.95 0 .751.751 0 0 1-.018 1.042.751.751 0 0 1-1.042.018 1.998 1.998 0 0 0-2.83 0l-2.5 2.5a1.998 1.998 0 0 0 0 2.83Z"></path></svg></a></div>
<p dir="auto">Turn the separator into NUL and use <code>-z</code>. For records separated by a <code>----</code> line:</p>
<div class="highlight highlight-source-shell notranslate position-relative overflow-auto" dir="auto" data-snippet-clipboard-copy-content="perl -0777 -pe 's/\n----\n/\0/g' notes.txt | sys1grep -z -e &quot;a decision was made&quot; | tr '\0' '\n'
awk '/^----$/ { printf &quot;%c&quot;, 0; next } { print }' notes.txt | sys1grep -z -e &quot;a decision was made&quot; | tr '\0' '\n'"><pre>perl -0777 -pe <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>s/\n----\n/\0/g<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span> notes.txt <span class="pl-k">|</span> sys1grep -z -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>a decision was made<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> <span class="pl-k">|</span> tr <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>\0<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span> <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>\n<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span>
awk <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>/^----$/ { printf "%c", 0; next } { print }<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span> notes.txt <span class="pl-k">|</span> sys1grep -z -e <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">"</span>a decision was made<span class="pl-pds">"</span></span> <span class="pl-k">|</span> tr <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>\0<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span> <span class="pl-s"><span class="pl-pds">'</span>\n<span class="pl-pds">'</span></span></pre></div>
<p dir="auto">NUL is what <code>git log -z</code>, <code>find -print0</code> and <code>xargs -0</code> already emit, so <code>-z</code> covers them directly (#6).
A general separator would bring escaping, multi-byte and regex-or-literal questions for a case one line of
<code>perl</code> or <code>awk</code> handles. The <code>awk</code> form works with the BSD awk on macOS, which does not take a
multi-character <code>RS</code>.</p>
